teaser.text: Prudential plc sells life and health insurance and manages investments, chiefly for customers in Asia and Africa. Its dollar comes in mainly through premiums and management fees, then goes out through claims, benefits, commissions, operating costs and the assets that support future promises.

stock.title: Prudential stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Prudential's forecast gives 1028.12 GBp in October 2027 and 1336.33 GBp in October 2029, weighted across 30% bear, 50% base and 20% bull cases.
stock.opening: Prudential's weighted scenario reaches 1028.12 GBp in October 2027. It hinges on policy growth converting into capital generation despite China-related risks.
stock.closing: The full memo also covers Prudential's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Prudential's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast points to a positive central outcome, but with a wide distribution of possible prices. The weighted price reaches 1028.12 GBp in October 2027, a 17% total return including dividends. It reaches 1159.17 GBp in October 2028, a 34% return. By October 2029, it reaches 1336.33 GBp, a 56% return.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Prudential's base case, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is 1,028.12 GBp in October 2027, a 17% total return. The forecast assigns 30% probability to bear, 50% to base and 20% to bull. Stronger agent productivity, bank distribution and customer retention support the case; mainland weakness or lower Hong Kong demand weaken it. The 5 November 2026 nine-month update tests sales and distribution. Completion of the enlarged buyback by 18 December 2026, India approvals and later remittances test whether expansion and payouts can be funded together. The case is growth becoming durable shareholder cash.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Prudential really make?

paragraphs.text: Free surplus shows how existing business releases capital. Prudential generated $3,059 million of operating free surplus from in-force insurance and asset-management business in 2025. After investment in new business, central costs and other expenditure, group operating free surplus was $1,675 million. It is a capital-generation measure, not accounting profit.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Prudential today?

paragraphs.text: Prudential’s headline price-to-earnings ratio, or P/E, makes the shares look inexpensive, but the quality of the earnings matters more than the label. A P/E compares the share price with annual earnings. Reported earnings include investment movements and the gain from selling part of the Indian asset manager in 2025, while core earnings are intended to show the continuing business more clearly.

dividend.title: Prudential dividend: payment and cash cover
dividend.meta_description: Prudential pays a rising dividend, with cash generation shaped by new business, central costs, buybacks and capital needs.
dividend.opening: Prudential paid 24.04 cents per share in dividends in 2025, alongside 48.30 cents of buybacks. Group operating generation was $1,154 million after new-business investment and central costs, while earnings retained after dividends and buybacks were $828 million.
dividend.closing: The full Prudential memo also explains Prudential's business, its rivals, its management choices and its risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Prudential pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Insurance revenue grew 7.0% in 2025 and the underwriting result rose, but operating return on equity stayed at 14.0% for three years. Diluted EPS was 153.50 cents in 2025, or about 104.31 cents without the transaction gain. Average diluted shares fell 4.7%; buybacks were 48.30 cents alongside 24.04 cents of dividends.

blocks.heading: Does Prudential's cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: That gross amount still funded growth and central costs. Prudential invested $383 million in new business and made further deductions for other expenditure and restructuring, leaving group operating generation at $1,154 million. Capability spending included $145 million on customers, distribution, health and technology. Rising expected releases alongside continued new-business investment is encouraging, although a specialist still asks whether capital is emerging from durable growth or temporary favourable experience.
**Kept to grow and build capital** — Without the $1,275 million after-tax transaction gain, mainly the Indian asset-manager sale, earnings retained after dividends and buybacks were $828 million.

paragraphs.text: Prudential could reach a weighted 1,336.33 GBp by October 2029, a 56% total return, if policy growth converts into capital generation despite China-related risks. Management targets 15%–20% annual compound growth in new business profit from 2022 to 2027. It also targets US$4.4 billion of operating free surplus generation from in-force business in 2027. For 2026, it targets 10% growth in new business profit, in-force operating free surplus generation and adjusted operating EPS, plus 10% annual dividend growth in 2026 and 2027.
